body:
Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/93495

I followed up with Editor testing on 
```
Godot v4.3.stable - Android - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Adreno (TM) 740 -  (8 Threads)
```
and Editor & Export testing on
```
Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8700K CPU @ 3.70GHz (12 Threads)
```

AXE.tres has a null value for `soundEffect`, `Sound Effect <Empty>`. The Editor does not respect the missing soundEffect override in the tscn as a null. And assigns the load value during a test run. 

On export AXE.tres is converted to AXE.res binary, which respects the null. The load is not assigned.

In the Editor, if an Item resource is created as a binary res, the null will be respected. No beep.

The AXE.tres, or other Item resources, being created without the assumed default sound is resolved by properly setting up the resource.

```
class_name Item
extends Resource

const DEFAULT_AUDIO : AudioStream = preload("res://pickup.wav")

@export var itemName: String
@export var soundEffect: AudioStream = DEFAULT_AUDIO
```

This will not fix existing .tres files of `Item` type that have missing soundEffect overrides.

There remains an issue between how .tres and .res `null` override values are treated differently.

I just ran into this issue yesterday. I tested on 4.3.stable and 4.4.rc1, the bug is present in both. 

It also applies to inline custom default resources as well:
```
class_name ParentResource extends Resource

@export var child_resource: ChildResource = ChildResource.new(500)
```

The editor shows null for `child_resource`, but works when running via the editor:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/893372fd-bbb8-4369-b696-533372818cdb)

The property `child_resource` is null when running via an exported project:
```
func _ready() -> void:
	print(parent_resource.child_resource.test_property)
	label.text = str(parent_resource.child_resource.test_property)
```

However, it seems to work perfectly fine when the default values are in an array:
```
class_name ParentResource extends Resource

# Null via exported project, but present running in editor
@export var child_resource: ChildResource = ChildResource.new(500)

# Present when running in editor and exported project
@export var child_resources: Array[ChildResource] = [
	ChildResource.new(1000)
]
```

Child resource:
```
class_name ChildResource extends Resource

@export var test_property: float

func _init(_test_property: float = 100):
	test_property = _test_property
```

The editor shows null for the `child_resources` array property in the editor:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b01995e7-48aa-454a-b1ec-20cbe5b428ba)

The `child_resources` value is present running via the editor and an exported project:
```
label_2.text = str(parent_resource.child_resources.front().test_property)
```

Additionally I noticed that `child_resources` array is explicitly set to null in the TestNode.tscn, while `child_resource` property isn't present at all. Attempting to add `child_resource` to the tscn does nothing as the editor clears it on save:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e25999d2-4fc7-4b01-b707-b10eadae5178)

Running in editor:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/322d61ac-aa70-42e7-ae4c-1e9113b205d8)

Running exported project:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68edb7e1-02d2-474a-a454-32b563304f29)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f907f8a-2b80-400f-837e-268d5b79349d)

Can confirm this issue fully persists through to 4.5beta3. I was able to repro it both on the original 4.3 stable as well as 4.5beta3 on arch/niri.

I did some further testing on 4.5dev3 and it looks like the actual resource itself has no reference to the actual file, and would have to refer to the base resource script to obtain it. When I tested this on ints and strings as well to see how it treated primitives, I found that they were working perfectly fine, despite not being present in the individual resources, like the audio files, and having to refer to their source, also like the audio files. 

For example if the int default was 4, any resources using that default (4) do not store that variable in their individual files, but only do so when its value is not equal to that default (eg: 347). The same is true for strings. Audio resources are identical in theory, however must be loaded, which oddly seems to occur locally but not when built. I reckon there's something that doesn't evaluate the load() or the new() functions above at some step in the build process leaving those resources empty. 

As a temporary workaround you could just pass in string file paths and load resources when they're needed using that string. 

Edit: bewilderingly, that array workaround mentioned above by @eburns1148 also works great for some reason, so that's more than likely a great place to start debugging.
Running into this as well in 4.6.1.stable.mono
